lines.en: A year later, a small line appeared beneath the sign: "Umbrellas lent free on rainy days — please return them. Or come back another day and share a pot of tea."
lines.zh: 一年后，门口的招牌下多了一行小字："雨天免费借伞，请记得还——或者，改天回来一起喝杯茶。"

lines.en: Every rainy evening someone pushes the door open to escape the rain, and the chime rings softly. You look up from behind the counter; he looks up from the stacks; and you smile at each other.
lines.zh: 每个下雨的傍晚，总有人推门进来避雨，风铃轻响。你在柜台后抬头，他从书堆里也抬起头，两个人相视一笑。

lines.en: The book of poems still sits in the most visible spot. There are three lines on the flyleaf now — the third one is yours: "I came. And I'm not leaving."
lines.zh: 那本诗集还摆在最显眼的地方。扉页上如今有三行字了——第三行是你写的："我来了。而且，不走了。"

lines.en: Dango rolls over lazily, claiming the patch of light that belongs to the two of you. The shop keeps its own hours now, and so do the two of you.
lines.zh: 团子懒洋洋地翻了个身，占着属于你们的那束光。这家店从今往后开到几点，你们两个说了算。

lines.en: The Kind of Love That Takes Its Time
He never said the whole sentence, and you never rushed him.
lines.zh: 他没有说出那句最完整的话，你也没有催。

lines.en: Some kinds of love are like old books — you turn them one page at a time.
lines.zh: 有些喜欢像旧书，要一页一页慢慢翻。

lines.en: Now you come every week: sorting books, feeding the cat, reading whole afternoons by the window. Neither of you has ever said it outright, but on the days you're due, he brews an extra pot of osmanthus oolong; and on the evenings he's swamped, you flip the 'Open' sign for him.
lines.zh: 如今你每周都来，帮他理书、喂猫、在窗边读一个下午。你们谁都没有正式说破，可他会在你要来的那天，多泡一壶桂花乌龙；你会在他忙不过来的傍晚，替他把'营业中'的牌子翻过来。

lines.en: "No rush," he says one day, looking at you, his ears still going pink. "I waited years for this shop. For you — I'm happy to take my time."
lines.zh: "不急，"有天他望着你说，耳根还是会红，"我等了这家店很多年。等你，我愿意慢慢来。"

lines.en: Outside, it starts to rain again. This time, you both have umbrellas. The shop keeps its own hours now, and so do the two of you.
lines.zh: 窗外又开始下雨了。这一次，你们都有伞。这家店从今往后开到几点，你们两个说了算。

lines.en: Only a Line Between the Pages
lines.zh: 夹在书里的，只是一句话

lines.en: Later you moved to another city.
lines.zh: 后来你搬去了别的城市。

lines.en: Before leaving, you visited the shop one last time. He was still there, and Dango, and that warm amber lamp. You put the book of poems back on the shelf and didn't take it with you.
lines.zh: 临走前你最后一次去了那家书店。他还在，团子还在，那盏暖黄的灯也还在。你把那本诗集放回架上，没有带走。

lines.en: "Travel safe," he said at the door, smiling softly — the same way he had the night he lent you the umbrella.
lines.zh: "路上小心。"他站在门口说，笑得很轻，像那晚借你伞时一样。

lines.en: Years on, you still think of that shop sometimes, and the faded line on the flyleaf.
lines.zh: 很多年后你偶尔会想起那家店，想起扉页上那行褪色的字。

lines.en: Some words, the moment they're written, already know they may not be for the one who stays. You just happened, once, to read them. The shop keeps its own hours now, and so do the two of you.
lines.zh: 有些话写下来的时候，就已经知道，未必是写给会留下来的人。你只是恰好，读到过。这家店从今往后开到几点，你们两个说了算。
